items.note: Genealogy in the record names Udayāditya, Naravarman, Yaśōvarman and Jayavarman in succession; relationship of first three from father to son known from other records.
Jayasimha Siddharāja annexed Paramāra kingdom, captured Yaśovarman; date Vikrama 1195, 9 June 1138 A.C., per his Ujjain inscription.
Chandēllas under Madanavarman had crossed the Betwā and annexed a considerable portion of Mālwā.
Kalachuri Gayākarṇa had married Alhanadēvī, the grand-daughter of Udayāditya.
After Jayasimha's death (V.S. 1200 or 1142-43 A.C.) Jayavarman re-occupied Mālwā.
Charter of Mahākumāra Lakshmīvarman confirming his predecessor Yasāvarman's grant at the annual funeral ceremonies of Naravarman, Vikrama 1191.
Lakshmīvarman's record names Udayādityadēva, his successor Naravarmadēva, then Yaśōvarmadēva, then Lakshmīvarman.
Grant of Vadaūda and Uthavanaka in the Mahādvādaśaka-maṇḍala confirmed in Vikrama 1200 (lunar eclipse).
Kielhorn's view of the succession in Yaśōvarman's family (Jayavarman, Ajayavarman, Lakshmīvarman); a scholarly debate on the Paramāra division.
Chandēlas had usurped a portion of the region around Bhilsā, per the Augasī grant of Madanavarman.
Summary: after Chaulukya Jayasinha captured Yaśōvarman in 1138 A.C., his sons left Dhāra for the Bhopāl region and annexed territory from the Chandellas.
Jayavarman resumed government at Dhāra as sovereign; Lakshmīvarman stayed in Bhopāl region with the lower title Mahākumāra.
The Mahādvādaśaka maṇḍala comprised parts of modern Bhilsā (Vidishā) and Bhopāl districts.
